title: Possible {name} in source
description: The file contains {name}. Anyone who can read the repository, image or build log can try the value against the same account until it is rotated. Shape-only: the match does not prove the password is live.
remediation: Rotate the password at the database or service it belongs to, review authentication logs for its use, and inject the replacement from a secret manager at run time instead of storing it in the tree.
limitation: Shape-only: the rule matches a credential-named key assigned a password-shaped literal (8+ characters with at least one digit). It cannot prove the value is live, current, or used by this system.
fp: Documentation samples, template placeholders and generated example configurations are the common false positives; the pattern requires 8+ characters and at least one digit, and vetoes EXAMPLE text.
recordDesc: {name} committed as a literal is readable by every account that can clone the repository and by every process that loads the configuration. Rotation is the only remedy once the value has been exposed.
applicability: Source files, .env files, CI configuration and container manifests that may embed {name}.
risk: Authenticated access to the datastore or service that accepts this password, with the privileges of its account; HIGH severity.
why: {name} kept in version control keeps working for whoever holds a copy of the file until someone rotates it.
fix: Rotate the password in the owning system now.
Search history, images and logs for the same value and purge or invalidate it there.
Store the replacement in a secret manager and reference it by name at deploy time.
verifyT: The old password no longer authenticates and no literal shaped like this rule remains in the working tree or history.
